questions.question: Describe how umqombothi is brewed, including why the sorghum is malted. Write the word equation for alcoholic fermentation and give two signs that a chemical reaction is taking place.
questions.expected_answer: Sorghum grains are soaked and left warm and damp to sprout (malting); enzymes in the sprouting grain break starch into sugars, then the grain is dried and ground into malt. The malt is mixed with cooked maize porridge and water and left in a warm place for two to three days; yeasts ferment the sugars without oxygen. Word equation: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide. Signs: bubbles of carbon dioxide and froth; a new sour or alcoholic smell and taste; the mixture becomes warm. Malting is needed because yeast cannot ferment starch directly.

questions.question: Explain how amasi is made and why it lasts longer than fresh milk. Give the word equation for lactic acid fermentation.
questions.expected_answer: Fresh milk is left in a calabash, clay pot or leather bag for a few days. Lactic acid bacteria in the milk and container ferment the milk sugar (lactose) into lactic acid: glucose (sugar) → lactic acid. The acid causes the milk proteins to clump together so the milk thickens into a sour curd; the whey is drained off. The acidity (low pH) prevents most harmful and spoilage bacteria from growing, so amasi keeps much longer than fresh milk without refrigeration.

questions.question: Describe how iron was smelted by early southern African communities. Explain the chemical reaction that produces iron and the purpose of charcoal and bellows.
questions.expected_answer: Clay furnaces were filled with layers of charcoal and crushed iron ore; air was pumped in through clay pipes by goatskin bellows. Charcoal (carbon) burns fiercely with the forced air, reaching over 1 000 °C, and with limited oxygen forms carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide removes oxygen from the iron oxide: iron oxide + carbon monoxide → iron + carbon dioxide. Unwanted rock melts as slag; iron collects as a spongy bloom that is reheated and hammered into tools. Charcoal supplies the carbon and heat; bellows supply oxygen to raise the temperature.
